node_definition.done_when: Read section 32 of crew-runtime-positive-controls and its two comments first. They hold the evidence: the reckon producer's last log row at 19:47:45Z, its lease renewed at 19:55:30Z, and an imas-ambix producer that completed its reload at 19:30:30Z and was gone by 20:22Z, after the follower that saw the reload was killed at 19:38:33Z. The current producer's stdio goes to its log file, not a pipe. Read the producer lifecycle in reckon/cli.py (the watch command, its lease and its os.execve reload), and read reckon/crew/runs.py without editing it, since another live run claims it. Check each candidate against the retained records: the follower lease and what renews it, a signal reaching the detached session, an exception swallowed before logging, and the reloaded image's handling of descriptors inherited across the exec. Record each with what ruled it in or out. State the cause in the manifest, with the evidence each claim rests on; a claim with no evidence is named as a hypothesis. Whatever the cause, a producer that stops for any reason writes one line to its log saying why before it exits, and a follower that finds the producer gone reports that line. tests/test_producer_says_why_it_stops.py drives a stop, asserts the line, and fails at the base. If the cause is reproduced, a second test drives it and asserts the producer keeps publishing. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: Find why the reckon and imas-ambix watch producers stopped silently after a completed reload, and make a stopping producer say why, as crew-runtime-positive-controls §32 states.
